parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define gravitational potential at a point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A satellite X, of mass *M*, orbits a planet at a constant distance 4*R* from the centre of the planet, as shown in Fig. 1.1.

[[fig:f1]]

A second satellite Y, of mass 2*M*, orbits the planet with orbital radius *R*.

The gravitational potential at X due to the planet is −*Φ*. The planet is a uniform sphere.
parts.text: Explain why the gravitational potential at X is negative.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State an expression, in terms of *Φ*, for the gravitational potential at Y due to the planet.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Complete Table 1.1 by giving expressions, in terms of some or all of *M*, *R* and *Φ*, for the quantities indicated for each of the satellites X and Y.

[[fig:f2]]

figures.caption: Fig. 1.1
figures.alt: A planet at the centre of two dashed circular orbits, with satellite Y on the inner orbit and satellite X on the outer orbit; radii R and 4R are marked.

figures.caption: Table 1.1
figures.alt: A table with columns for satellite X and satellite Y and rows for gravitational field strength at the satellite due to the planet and gravitational potential energy of the satellite.
